title: Energy pyramids
examples: Teacher, why are the top levels always smaller?
How much energy is lost when energy moves up the food chain?
Can you show me an example of an energy pyramid in a desert?

explain.say: Today we look at energy pyramids in nature.

items: Primary Consumers: Herbivores eat the plants
Secondary Consumers: Carnivores eat the herbivores
Tertiary Consumers: Top predators eat the secondary consumers

explain.say: Producers are the base of every energy pyramid.
Primary consumers eat the producers for energy.
Secondary consumers eat the primary consumers next.
Top predators are at the very peak of the pyramid.

draw.text: Top Predators: Apex of the food chain

explain.say: Only about ten percent of energy moves up each level.

faq.q: Why is the pyramid shape always getting smaller at the top?
faq.a: Because a lot of energy is lost as heat or used for life processes.
asks: Why are there fewer top predators?
What causes the pyramid to narrow?
Does energy disappear when it moves up?

faq.q: What does the ten percent rule mean for energy?
faq.a: It means that only about one tenth of the energy from one level reaches the next level.
asks: How much energy is actually passed on?
Does the energy amount decrease steadily?

faq.q: Are producers always the largest part of the pyramid?
faq.a: Yes, producers form the base because they capture the initial energy source, usually sunlight.
asks: Why are plants at the bottom?
Can something other than plants be the base?

faq.q: Does the type of ecosystem change the pyramid shape?
faq.a: Yes, some ecosystems, like those with detritus, might have different pyramid shapes.
asks: Does the environment matter for energy flow?
Can the base be something other than plants?
What if there are no visible plants?

faq.q: What is the difference between energy and biomass?
faq.a: Biomass is the total mass of living organisms at one time, which is different from the energy flow.
asks: Are energy and mass the same thing?
Is biomass measured in energy units?
How do I measure the size of a trophic level?

facts: Producers, like plants, capture energy from the sun.
Energy moves from one trophic level to the next.
Only about ten percent of energy is transferred at each level.
Top predators are at the highest, smallest level of the pyramid.

quiz.say: If producers have 10,000 units of energy, the primary consumers will receive:
quiz.why: The ten percent rule means you divide the starting energy by ten.

wrong.1: This assumes all the energy is passed on, which is incorrect.
wrong.2: This would be dividing by one hundred, not ten.
wrong.3: This suggests energy multiplies, which violates the law of conservation.

quiz.say: Which group forms the base of the energy pyramid?
quiz.why: Producers are the first organisms to capture energy from the sun.

wrong.0: Top predators are at the end of the energy flow.
wrong.1: Decomposers break down waste, but they are not the initial energy source.
wrong.3: Primary consumers must eat something first to get energy.

quiz.say: If a secondary consumer has 100 units of energy, the tertiary consumer will have:
quiz.why: The energy transfer is consistently ten percent at each step up.

wrong.0: This is too low; it ignores the initial ten percent transfer.
wrong.1: This represents a fifty percent loss, not the standard ten percent rule.
wrong.3: This suggests energy increases, which is impossible in a closed system.
